title: Tim Cook Stepping Down as Apple CEO
excerpt: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years leading the company, becoming executive chairman as John Ternus takes over as CEO.

title: U.S. vs Iran: The War Has Escalated Again
excerpt: Fighting between the U.S. and Iran intensified again in early September 2026, with new airstrikes near the Strait of Hormuz pushing oil prices higher and raising fears of wider escalation.

title: Cassandra Wilson Death: Jazz Legend Passes at 70
excerpt: Grammy-winning jazz singer Cassandra Wilson has died at 70 in her hometown of Jackson, Mississippi. A two-time Grammy winner and NEA Jazz Master, she helped redefine jazz singing.

title: Tornado Warning Issued: What's Happening Right Now and Who Is at Risk?
excerpt: Severe storms brought tornado warnings to Michigan and nearby Great Lakes areas in early September 2026. Here's the difference between a warning and a watch, and what to do right now.

title: FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026: Action Underway in Berlin
excerpt: The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 is underway in Berlin, with Team USA, Caitlin Clark, and 15 other nations chasing the title from September 4-13.

title: McDonald's India X Account Controversy: What Happened
excerpt: Unusual posts appeared on McDonald's India's official X account claiming unpaid intern wages before being deleted. McDonald's India later suggested the posts were fake; the claims remain unverified.

title: LISA's “SaWaDiKa” Official Music Video: A Bold Hello from Thailand
excerpt: LISA of BLACKPINK's new single “SaWaDiKa” hit 70.8 million views in 24 hours and 100 million in two days, celebrating her Thai roots ahead of her Press Play EP.

title: Canada's Retaliatory Tariffs on U.S. Goods Take Effect
excerpt: Canada's counter-tariffs on $27.6 billion of U.S. goods took effect September 8, 2026, matching new U.S. duties dollar for dollar across steel, dairy, appliances, and other sectors.

title: Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026: All the Big News in Simple Words
excerpt: Nintendo's September 9, 2026 Direct revealed Metroid Ravenous and Kirby and the World Beyond for Switch 2, plus a huge wave of third-party games including Monster Hunter Wilds and Final Fantasy VII Revelation.

title: Apple “Surprise and Shine” Event: iPhone Duo and All the New Products Explained Simply
excerpt: Apple's September 9, 2026 event unveiled the foldable iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5, led by new CEO John Ternus.

title: Remembering September 11: The 25th Anniversary of a Day That Changed the World
excerpt: Today, September 11, 2026, marks 25 years since the September 11, 2001 attacks. This year's commemoration adds a new seventh moment of silence honoring those who later died from related illnesses.

title: BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi: What You Need to Know in Simple Words
excerpt: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, bringing together leaders including Putin, Xi Jinping, and Pezeshkian under the theme of resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.

title: Alexander Zverev Wins the 2026 US Open Men's Title
excerpt: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 at Arthur Ashe Stadium to win his first US Open and second Grand Slam title of 2026, the first German man to win in New York since Boris Becker.

title: Apple Releases iOS 27 with Major Siri AI Overhaul
excerpt: Apple released iOS 27 on September 14, 2026, headlined by Siri AI — a rebuilt assistant with natural conversation, personal context, and a dedicated app — plus Liquid Glass controls and new photo tools.

title: Kennedy Center Board Votes to Close Building for Renovations
excerpt: The Kennedy Center board voted on September 15, 2026 to immediately close its main building for a two-year, roughly $250 million renovation, citing safety and financial concerns amid an ongoing legal dispute over the building's name.

title: US House Votes to End Iran War for Third Time
excerpt: The US House voted 220-204 on September 15, 2026 to pass a war powers resolution on Iran, with seven Republicans joining all Democrats. It is the third such House vote this year.

title: Federal Reserve Raises Interest Rates for First Time Since 2023
excerpt: The Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate by 0.25% on September 16, 2026, bringing the target range to 3.75%–4% — the first hike since July 2023, citing inflation tied to higher energy prices linked to the war involving Iran.

title: Iran's IRGC Claims Strike on Togo-Flagged Oil Tanker in Strait of Hormuz
excerpt: Iran's IRGC said it struck the Togo-flagged oil tanker Trend in the Strait of Hormuz on September 18, 2026, sparking a fire. UKMTO separately reported a security incident nearby, with the crew safe and no confirmed environmental damage.

title: Trump Announces US Security Deal on Greenland Called “Infinite Life” Agreement
excerpt: President Trump announced a proposed “Infinite Life” security agreement with Denmark and Greenland on September 18, 2026, giving the US long-term basing, access, and overflight rights with no cost or end date, expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.

title: 20th Asian Games Open in Nagoya, Japan
excerpt: The 20th Asian Games officially began on September 19, 2026, in Nagoya, Japan, with Emperor Naruhito declaring the Games open and over 15,000 athletes from 45 nations competing in 43 sports for 469 gold medals through October 4.

title: Trump Says He Is in “Deciding Mode” on Iran and Warns of “Very Big Things” as Tehran Issues Seven Conditions
excerpt: On September 20, 2026, Trump said he is in “deciding mode” on Iran, weighing military action, economic pressure, or a deal, as Tehran sent seven conditions for talks through Qatari mediators, including an end to fighting and the US naval blockade.

title: Scientists Find the Human Brain May Be Two Separate Organs
excerpt: A new Stanford study, published in Nature Neuroscience in mid-September 2026, suggests the human brain developed from two separate groups of embryonic cells — one forming the forebrain/midbrain and the other the hindbrain/brainstem — with ancient evolutionary origins.

title: First Stellar Stream Found Beyond the Milky Way
excerpt: Astronomers have discovered the first clear stellar stream from a globular cluster outside the Milky Way, named Oyashio, in the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1 about 115 million light-years away, giving scientists a new way to measure dark matter in distant galaxies.

title: AI Finds a Mysterious DNA Enzyme System on Its Own
excerpt: An AI system called Claude, made by Anthropic, helped scientists discover a previously unnoticed biological system called ART (array-associated reverse transcriptases). About 950 AI agents searched over 200,000 enzymes and found a CRISPR-like pattern, later confirmed in the lab.
